ratings_why.fun: One Lamp dial gives two opposite builds, stop at 7 or blow past it, and each cast is a small push-your-luck call; the thin early game and the exact-7 arithmetic keep it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: A threshold dial that pays both for hitting it and for overshooting it, carried into the fight, plays unlike any of today's tribes; spell-count scaling itself is familiar.

verdict_why: Mostly reads cleanly, but The Old Lady's limit needs to say whether it covers fights, and the Hawk-moth's order gives a confusing zero.

points.text: The Old Lady says "Once a turn", but Flares also happen in fights and Bramble's limits are per turn or per fight. Say whether she stops an in-fight Flare, for example "Once a turn and once a fight".
Eyed Hawk-moth Stokes first, so at Heat 7 its own Stoke Flares, Heat drops to 0 and the attacker loses nothing. Reading Heat before the Stoke would match what a player expects.
The flame fantasy reads in play: moths creep toward the Flashpoint, the Old Lady snuffs, the Lamp bursts. Showing the dial on the board with the Flashpoint marked would carry the whole tribe.
The Herald is a bare Stoke 3; something that ties to announcing the season, such as Stoking more on the turn you Tier up, would give it the moth's character.

Old Carbonaria adds a second counter, Heat gained this turn, and her text doesn't use the peppered moth's colour change. A version that swaps between Simmer and Flare payouts would read as her and drop the extra counter.

standouts.why: The Old Lady is a safety valve for one build and a sell decision for the other, in one short line.
Dame Pavonia never eating becomes Can't gain stats, a clear drawback that is pure seed.
Eyed Hawk-moth flashing its eyes to weaken the attacker is the moth's real trick, read at a glance.

weakest.why: The Herald is a plain Heat battery with no character in its text.
Lamp-Fanner is a pure enabler with no stats of its own, a dull buy before Tier 4.
The Uncertain never sure of a dose would suit a random Phial size; a plain Phial a turn hides the joke.

flags.note: Doesn't say whether "Once a turn" covers Flares during the fight.
At Flashpoint 3 with Mother Shipton and Burnt-Ring Senior, in-fight Flares could fire every few hits, each a permanent board buff.
Pavonia doubling Old Carbonaria is the designer's own high roll; worth the owner's eye.
